key_insight: A machine learning model can identify early-stage node-negative breast cancer patients at higher relapse risk and remains moderately accurate across two independent cohorts.
clinical_relevance: If validated further, this could help clinicians better target adjuvant chemotherapy and avoid overtreatment in lower-risk patients.
method: Trained and tested models on MSK-IMPACT and METABRIC node-negative stage I-II breast cancer cohorts.
Evaluated three settings: within-cohort cross-validation and cross-cohort transfer in both directions.
Used sensitivity analysis, data harmonization, survival analysis, SHAP, and ablation testing to assess robustness and interpretability.
evidence_signal: The combined-cohort model achieved AUC 0.788 ± 0.028 in five-fold cross-validation, with cross-cohort AUCs of 0.741 and 0.714, and showed significant survival separation on METABRIC.
watch_item: Performance was lower when models were transferred between cohorts, so external validation and careful harmonization are still needed before clinical use.
paper_title: Cross-cohort generalizability of machine learning models for early-stage node-negative breast cancer relapse prediction
